title: Snellen screening toy
text:
What it is
A webcam eye test you can run on your own computer. It shows a chart of classic Snellen letters, “Tumbling E” shapes or Landolt C rings, sizes them to how far you are from the screen, and tests each eye in turn.
The demo runs entirely in the browser: the camera stays on your device and no video is uploaded. It needs a webcam and a bank card (or any card the same size), which is used as a ruler to measure the screen and calibrate the camera.

title: Snellen screening toy
text:
What I built
Rapid deployable eye testing is still stuck in the 20th Century, with most online Snellen tests requiring a tape measure, a television sized screen, rock-steady seating, and a second pair of hands.
This project aimed to use a computer vision solution so lightweight that it could run in-browser, with the added benefit of keeping all patient data on their own device, so no strict patient confidentiality to worry about.

title: Snellen screening toy
text:
How it works

The same Python package runs on the desktop and in the browser. In the browser, Pyodide runs it with numpy and OpenCV.
MediaPipe’s Face Landmarker tracks the face; a bank card, held to the screen and then to the forehead, gives the scale for the screen and the camera.
Chart sizes come from the same geometry code in all versions, in device pixels, and font resizes dynamically as the patients’ head changes distance from the screen.

title: Receipt OCR
text:
What it is
Petty-cash receipts for a group of restaurants. Staff photograph receipts, Claude reads the shop, date and total, staff check and tag each one, and a manager emails the month’s ledger as an xlsx file to the head of department.
It runs locally as a small web app for now; AWS comes next.

title: Receipt OCR
text:
What I built
Many small businesses in Japan still operate their monthly budgeting using data manually entered by fatigued shop employees who often aren’t trained in spreadsheet formats and standards, leading to the digital equivalent of a hoarder’s cluttered file system.
This project aimed to address these pain points in the simplest manner possible to reduce error at the entry stage by employees, and to reduce the headache for managers who would often spend hours untangling a spreadsheet that has had its formatting and save encoding ruined by inconsistent software across multiple computers.

title: Receipt OCR
text:
How it works

A model (Claude Haiku or Sonnet) extracts the shop, date and total from each photo, and the result is validated before staff see it.
An evaluation command scores the extractors against hand-labelled sample photos.
